Then write the validation script. Pure stdlib:

```python
import struct, math

HDR = 272
data = open(path,'rb').read()
recs = []
off = 0
while off + HDR <= len(data):
    (csiDataSize, space4, ftmClock) = struct.unpack_from('<III', data, off)
    (timestamp,) = struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, off+12)
    numRx = data[off+46]; numTx = data[off+47]
    (numSubCarriers,) = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, off+52)
    (rssi1,) = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, off+60)
    (rssi2,) = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, off+64)
    srcMac = data[off+68:off+74]
    (rateNflag,) = struct.unpack_from('<I', data, off+92)
    payload = data[off+HDR : off+HDR+csiDataSize]
    ...
```

Checks:
1. file size == HDR + csiDataSize for the single record (720 == 272 + 448 ✓ expected).
2. payload size == numRx*numTx*numSubCarriers*4.
3. Decode rateNflag: format bits 8-10, width bits 11-13.
4. CSI samples: unpack 56*2*1 int16 pairs, compute magnitudes, phase.

7	On 2026-09-19, the Zenbook AX210 completed a FeitCSI `measureinject` smoke test at 2412 MHz / 20 MHz. It decoded one HT CSI frame with 56 subcarriers, 2 RX, and 1 TX, writing a complete 720-byte record.
8	
9	**Why:** This validates the driver, debugfs CSI control, and FeitCSI capture pipeline end to end on the test host.
10	
11	**How to apply:** Treat CSI availability as proven, but do not infer a usable fall-detection sampling rate from this test; validate passive capture and sustained transmitter traffic separately.

Validation is done — and it turned up a significant finding. Here's where things stand under the reduced scope (collect → validate → visualize):

## 1. Validation: the smoke capture is real, physical CSI

I wrote a dependency-free parser (`/tmp/validate_csi.py`, mirrors FeitCSI's own struct/decode logic) since numpy is still not installed. The 720-byte capture passes every check:

- **Structure**: record framing exact (272-byte header + 448-byte payload, no trailing bytes); payload size matches `numRx(2) × numTx(1) × numSubcarriers(56) × 4` precisely
- **Physical plausibility**: magnitudes non-degenerate (10–377, mean 130), edge subcarriers weaker than core on both RX chains (guard/DC null behavior of genuine HT-20 CSI), phases spread over the full ±π range (real multipath, not synthetic)
- **Header decode**: HT format, 20 MHz, RSSI 77/78 — all consistent with the verbose log

## 2. The big discovery: that frame was NOT ours — passive capture already proven

The header contradicts everything we injected:

| Field | We injected (~80 frames) | Captured CSI frame |
|---|---|---|
| MCS | 0 | **3** |
| Guard interval | 400 ns SGI | **long GI** |
| Coding | LDPC | **BCC** |
| srcMac | 00:11:22:33:44:55 | **68:72:51:58:79:97** |

I verified the injection path sends the rate verbatim (`PacketInjector.cpp:78-86`), so this isn't a decode artifact. Of ~80 self-injections, **zero** produced CSI — the single frame we captured was **passively overheard from an external transmitter** on channel 1 (two external APs are active there: "Maryam Nawaz free internet", "10"). That answers the runbook's riskiest assumption (Phase 3) affirmatively: **this AX210 + driver stack attaches CSI to arbitrary third-party frames**, no active link needed.

CSI "waterfall" of that frame (per-RX, subcarrier 0→55, ▓ = pilot):
```
rx0 |H|: ▅▅▅▅▅▆▆▓▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▓▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▆▓▅▅▅▅▅▅▆▆▆▆▆▅▆▓▅▅▅▅▅▅▅
rx1 |H|: ▂▂▂▂▂▁▂▓▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▓▁▁▁▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▓▂▃▃▃▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▓▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
```
Note rx1 shows a classic frequency-selective notch (subcarriers ~13–20) — textbook multipath signature.

## 3. What this changes

- `measureinject` is now known to be a **dead end for data collection** (self-injections produce no CSI) — passive `-i measure` is the way, and it works
- The remaining blocker for the *collection* step is unchanged though: your own transmitter. I won't deliberately capture neighbors' traffic. To collect a real dataset I still need you to name your AP from the scan (or say which device will transmit), and ideally run sustained traffic from it (`iperf3`/fast ping/download) during the capture

## 4. Visualization status

- Done for now: the ASCII plots above (stdlib-only)
- Better options, both pending: live GUI waterfall during capture (`sudo ./bin/app -x -p -f <freq> -w 20`) — no numpy needed, and post-hoc matplotlib plots via `feitcsi_parse.py` — needs `sudo apt install -y python3-numpy python3-matplotlib`

**Next step is yours**: name your AP's SSID or frequency from the scan (plus which device will transmit), and I'll hand you the exact passive-capture command. If you want visualization capability ready first, run the numpy/matplotlib install and I'll produce real plots from whatever we capture.

```json
{
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Dependency-free validation of a FeitCSI .dat capture.\n\nMirrors FeitCSI's own decoding (include/Csi.h RawHeaderData, src/Csi.cpp\nformat/width decode) using only the Python stdlib.\n\"\"\"\nimport math\nimport struct\nimport sys\n\nHDR = 272\n\nMOD_TYPES = {0: \"CCK\", 1: \"LEGACY_OFDM\", 2: \"HT\", 3: \"VHT\", 4: \"HE\", 5: \"EHT\"}\nWIDTHS = {0: 20, 1: 40, 2: 80, 3: 160, 4: 320}\nHT20_PILOTS = {7, 21, 34, 48}\n\n\ndef parse(path):\n    data = open(path, \"rb\").read()\n    print(f\"File: {path}\")\n    print(f\"Size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n\n    records = []\n    off = 0\n    while off + HDR <= len(data):\n        csi_size, _space4, ftm_clock = struct.unpack_from(\"<III\", data, off)\n        (timestamp,) = struct.unpack_from(\"<Q\", data, off + 12)\n        num_rx = data[off + 46]\n        num_tx = data[off + 47]\n        (num_sc,) = struct.unpack_from(\"<I\", data, off + 52)\n        (rssi1,) = struct.unpack_from(\"<I\", data, off + 60)\n        (rssi2,) = struct.unpack_from(\"<I\", data, off + 64)\n        src_mac = data[off + 68 : off + 74]\n        (rate_n_flags,) = struct.unpack_from(\"<I\", data, off + 92)\n\n        payload = data[off + HDR : off + HDR + csi_size]\n        records.append(\n            dict(\n                csi_size=csi_size,\n                ftm_clock=ftm_clock,\n                timestamp=timestamp,\n                num_rx=num_rx,\n                num_tx=num_tx,\n                num_sc=num_sc,\n                rssi1=rssi1,\n                rssi2=rssi2,\n                src_mac=src_mac,\n                rate_n_flags=rate_n_flags,\n                payload=payload,\n            )\n        )\n        off += HDR + csi_size\n\n    print(f\"Records: {len(records)}, trailing bytes: {len(data) - off}\")\n    return records\n\n\ndef decode_rate(rnf):\n    mod = (rnf >> 8) & 0x7\n    width = (rnf >> 11) & 0x7\n    mcs = rnf & 0xF\n    nss = (rnf >> 4) & 0x1\n    ldpc = bool(rnf & (1 << 27))\n    return MOD_TYPES.get(mod, f\"?{mod}\"), WIDTHS.get(width, f\"?{width}\"), mcs, nss, ldpc\n\n\ndef samples(rec):\n    \"\"\"int16 re/im pairs, order rx -> tx -> subcarrier (per Csi.h comment).\"\"\"\n    n = len(rec[\"payload\"]) // 4\n    vals = struct.unpack(f\"<{n*2}h\", rec[\"payload\"])\n    out = []\n    for i in range(0, len(vals), 2):\n        out.append(complex(vals[i], vals[i + 1]))\n    return out\n\n\ndef bar(v, maxv, width=56):\n    return \"#\" * max(0, min(width, round(v / maxv * width)))\n\n\ndef main(path):\n    records = parse(path)\n    for idx, rec in enumerate(records):\n        fmt, width, mcs, nss, ldpc = decode_rate(rec[\"rate_n_flags\"])\n        mac = \":\".join(f\"{b:02x}\" for b in rec[\"srcMac\"])\n        expected = rec[\"num_rx\"] * rec[\"num_tx\"] * rec[\"num_sc\"] * 4\n        print(f\"\\n--- Record {idx} ---\")\n        print(f\"  srcMac          : {mac}\")\n        print(f\"  timestamp       : {rec['timestamp']} ({rec['timestamp'] / 1e6:.3f} s)\"\n              if rec[\"timestamp\"] > 1e9 else\n              f\"  timestamp       : {rec['timestamp']}\")\n        print(f\"  numRx/numTx     : {rec['num_rx']} / {rec['num_tx']}\")\n        print(f\"  numSubCarriers  : {rec['num_sc']}\")\n        print(f\"  rssi1 / rssi2   : {rec['rssi1']} / {rec['rssi2']}\")\n        print(f\"  rateNFlags      : 0x{rec['rate_n_flags']:08x}\"\n              f\"  -> format={fmt} width={width}MHz mcs={mcs} nss={nss} ldpc={ldpc}\")\n        print(f\"  csiDataSize     : {rec['csi_size']} bytes\"\n              f\" (expected rx*tx*sc*4 = {expected}) -> \"\n              f\"{'OK' if expected == rec['csi_size'] else 'MISMATCH'}\")\n\n        smp = samples(rec)\n        mags = [abs(s) for s in smp]\n        nonzero = [m for m in mags if m > 0]\n        print(f\"  samples         : {len(smp)} complex int16\")\n        print(f\"  magnitude       : min={min(mags):.1f} max={max(mags):.1f} \"\n              f\"mean={sum(mags)/len(mags):.1f} zero-samples={len(mags)-len(nonzero)}\")\n        if not nonzero:\n            print(\"  !! all-zero CSI payload\")\n            continue\n\n        # edge-null check: HT/VHT 20 MHz reports 56 subcarriers, indices 0-3 and\n        # 52-55 are guard/DC nulls and should be ~0 in real channel data\n        per_rx = rec[\"num_sc\"]\n        for rx in range(rec[\"num_rx\"]):\n            rxm = mags[rx * per_rx : (rx + 1) * per_rx]\n            edge = rxm[:4] + rxm[-4:]\n            core = rxm[4:-4]\n            print(f\"  rx{rx}: edge-null mean={sum(edge)/len(edge):.1f} \"\n                  f\"core mean={sum(core)/len(core):.1f} \"\n                  f\"({'edge < core: consistent with real HT-20 CSI' if sum(edge) < sum(core) else 'NO edge suppression'})\")\n\n        # ASCII magnitude plot per rx (normalised to that rx's max)\n        for rx in range(rec[\"num_rx\"]):\n            rxm = mags[rx * per_rx : (rx + 1) * per_rx]\n            mx = max(rxm) or 1\n            print(f\"\\n  |H| rx{rx} (subcarrier 0..{per_rx-1}, '#'={mx:.0f})\")\n            for i, m in enumerate(rxm):\n                mark = \" P\" if i in HT20_PILOTS and fmt == \"HT\" and per_rx == 56 else \"\"\n                print(f\"   {i:3d} |{bar(m, mx)}{mark}\")\n\n        # phase sanity: phases should be spread (real multipath), not constant\n        for rx in range(rec[\"num_rx\"]):\n            rxp = [math.atan2(s.imag, s.real) for s in\n                   smp[rx * per_rx : (rx + 1) * per_rx] if s != 0]\n            if rxp:\n                print(f\"  rx{rx}: phase range {min(rxp):+.2f}..{max(rxp):+.2f} rad \"\n                      f\"({len(rxp)} non-null)\")\n\n    print(\"\\nDONE\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
```
2	"""
3	feitcsi_parse.py — Parse FeitCSI .dat binary captures into NumPy (.npz) / CSV.
4	
5	Binary format (verified against FeitCSI source: include/Csi.h + src/Csi.cpp):
6	
7	  The .dat file is a plain concatenation of records. Each record is:
8	      [ 272-byte RawHeaderData header ][ csiDataSize bytes of CSI payload ]
9	  Csi::save() opens the file in append mode and writes header+payload per frame,
10	  so records sit back-to-back with no separators.
11	
12	  Header struct is __attribute__((__packed__)) and x86 little-endian.
13	  Payload = csiDataSize/4 complex samples; each sample is 4 bytes:
14	      int16 LE real, int16 LE imag          (Csi::processRawCsi)
15	  magnitude = abs(real + j*imag); phase = atan2(imag, real).
16	
17	  Sample ordering (Csi::unwrapPhase / fixCsiBug loops are rx -> tx -> subcarrier):
18	      flat_index = (rx * numTx + tx) * numSubCarriers + subcarrier
19	
20	Header layout (offset, size, field, type):
21	   0   4   csiDataSize     uint32
22	   4   4   space4          uint32
23	   8   4   ftmClock        uint32
24	  12   8   timestamp       uint64   (device units; driver commonly microseconds)
25	  20  26   space20         bytes
26	  46   1   numRx           uint8
27	  47   1   numTx           uint8
28	  48   4   space48         bytes
29	  52   4   numSubCarriers  uint32
30	  56   4   space54         bytes
31	  60   4   rssi1           uint32
32	  64   4   rssi2           uint32
33	  68   6   srcMac          bytes
34	  74  18   space75         bytes
35	  92   4   rateNflag       uint32
36	  96 176   space96         bytes
37	  -----------------------------
38	  = 272 bytes (CSI_HEADER_LENGTH)
39	
40	rateNflag decode (lib/include/rs.h):
41	  format        = (rateNflag & 0x700)  >> 8    0=CCK 1=LEGACY_OFDM 2=HT 3=VHT 4=HE 5=EHT
42	  channel_width = (rateNflag & 0x3800) >> 11   0=20 1=40 2=80 3=160 4=320 (MHz)
43	
44	Usage:
45	  python3 feitcsi_parse.py capture.dat                 # -> capture.npz
46	  python3 feitcsi_parse.py capture.dat --info          # print summary, write nothing
47	  python3 feitcsi_parse.py capture.dat --csv           # also write tidy long CSV
48	  python3 feitcsi_parse.py capture.dat --drop-pilots   # remove pilot subcarriers
49	  python3 feitcsi_parse.py capture.dat -o run1         # output prefix = run1.*
50	
51	Requires: numpy (stdlib for everything else).
52	"""

63	# --- Header definition -------------------------------------------------------
64	
65	CSI_HEADER_LENGTH = 272
66	
67	# <  = little-endian, standard sizes, NO alignment/padding (matches __packed__)
68	_HEADER_FMT = "<IIIQ26sBB4sI4sII6s18sI176s"
69	_HEADER = struct.Struct(_HEADER_FMT)
70	assert _HEADER.size == CSI_HEADER_LENGTH, (
71	    f"header struct is {_HEADER.size} bytes, expected {CSI_HEADER_LENGTH}"
72	)
73	
74	_FORMAT_NAMES = {0: "CCK", 1: "LEGACY_OFDM", 2: "HT", 3: "VHT", 4: "HE", 5: "EHT"}
75	_WIDTH_NAMES = {0: 20, 1: 40, 2: 80, 3: 160, 4: 320}
76	
77	_RATE_MCS_MOD_TYPE_MSK = 0x7 << 8       # 0x700
78	_RATE_MCS_CHAN_WIDTH_MSK = 0x7 << 11    # 0x3800
79	
80	# Pilot subcarrier indices, keyed by (format_name, width_mhz). From Csi.h.
81	# LEGACY_OFDM uses the NOHT table; HT and VHT share tables; HE has its own.
82	_PILOT_INDICES = {
83	    ("LEGACY_OFDM", 20): [5, 19, 32, 46],
84	    ("HT", 20): [7, 21, 34, 48],
85	    ("HT", 40): [5, 33, 47, 66, 80, 108],
86	    ("VHT", 20): [7, 21, 34, 48],
87	    ("VHT", 40): [5, 33, 47, 66, 80, 108],
88	    ("VHT", 80): [19, 47, 83, 111, 130, 158, 194, 222],
89	    ("VHT", 160): [19, 47, 83, 111, 130, 158, 194, 222,
90	                   261, 289, 325, 353, 372, 400, 436, 464],
91	    ("HE", 20): [6, 32, 74, 100, 141, 167, 209, 235],
92	    ("HE", 40): [6, 32, 74, 100, 140, 166, 208, 234,
93	                 249, 275, 317, 343, 383, 409, 451, 477],
94	    ("HE", 80): [32, 100, 166, 234, 274, 342, 408, 476,
95	                 519, 587, 653, 721, 761, 829, 895, 963],
96	    ("HE", 160): [32, 100, 166, 234, 274, 342, 408, 476, 519, 587, 653, 721,
97	                  761, 829, 895, 963, 1028, 1096, 1162, 1230, 1270, 1338,
98	                  1404, 1472, 1515, 1583, 1649, 1717, 1757, 1825, 1891, 1959],
99	}

102	@dataclass
103	class Frame:
104	    """One decoded CSI record."""
105	    index: int
106	    timestamp: int
107	    src_mac: bytes
108	    num_rx: int
109	    num_tx: int
110	    num_subcarriers: int
111	    rssi1: int
112	    rssi2: int
113	    rate_n_flag: int
114	    format_code: int
115	    width_code: int
116	    csi_data_size: int
117	    # complex samples reshaped to (num_rx, num_tx, num_subcarriers); flat frames
118	    # that don't factor cleanly are stored as (1, 1, n_samples).
119	    csi: np.ndarray
120	
121	    @property
122	    def format_name(self) -> str:
123	        return _FORMAT_NAMES.get(self.format_code, f"UNKNOWN({self.format_code})")
124	
125	    @property
126	    def width_mhz(self) -> int:
127	        return _WIDTH_NAMES.get(self.width_code, 0)
128	
129	    @property
130	    def src_mac_str(self) -> str:
131	        return ":".join(f"{b:02x}" for b in self.src_mac)
132	
133	    @property
134	    def magnitude(self) -> np.ndarray:
135	        return np.abs(self.csi)
136	
137	    @property
138	    def phase(self) -> np.ndarray:
139	        return np.angle(self.csi)
140	
141	
142	def _decode_payload(payload: bytes, num_rx: int, num_tx: int,
143	                    num_subcarriers: int, verbose: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:
144	    """Turn raw payload bytes into a complex array shaped (rx, tx, subcarrier)."""
145	    n_samples = len(payload) // 4
146	    i16 = np.frombuffer(payload[: n_samples * 4], dtype="<i2")
147	    real = i16[0::2].astype(np.float64)
148	    imag = i16[1::2].astype(np.float64)
149	    csi = real + 1j * imag
150	
151	    expected = num_rx * num_tx * num_subcarriers
152	    if expected == n_samples and expected > 0:
153	        return csi.reshape(num_rx, num_tx, num_subcarriers)
154	
155	    if verbose:
156	        print(f"  [warn] payload has {n_samples} samples but header implies "
157	              f"{num_rx}x{num_tx}x{num_subcarriers}={expected}; storing flat",
158	              file=sys.stderr)
159	    return csi.reshape(1, 1, n_samples)
160	
161	
162	def parse_dat(path: str, verbose: bool = False) -> list:
163	    """Read every record in a FeitCSI .dat file. Returns a list of Frame."""
164	    frames = []
165	    size = os.path.getsize(path)
166	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
167	        idx = 0
168	        while True:
169	            header = f.read(CSI_HEADER_LENGTH)
170	            if len(header) == 0:
171	                break  # clean EOF
172	            if len(header) < CSI_HEADER_LENGTH:
173	                print(f"[warn] trailing {len(header)} bytes ignored (partial header)",
174	                      file=sys.stderr)
175	                break
176	
177	            (csi_data_size, _space4, _ftm_clock, timestamp, _space20,
178	             num_rx, num_tx, _space48, num_subcarriers, _space54,
179	             rssi1, rssi2, src_mac, _space75, rate_n_flag, _space96) = _HEADER.unpack(header)
180	
181	            if csi_data_size == 0 or csi_data_size > size:
182	                print(f"[warn] frame {idx}: implausible csiDataSize={csi_data_size}; stopping",
183	                      file=sys.stderr)
184	                break
185	
186	            payload = f.read(csi_data_size)
187	            if len(payload) < csi_data_size:
188	                print(f"[warn] frame {idx}: truncated payload "
189	                      f"({len(payload)}/{csi_data_size}); stopping", file=sys.stderr)
190	                break
191	
192	            csi = _decode_payload(payload, num_rx, num_tx, num_subcarriers, verbose)
193	            frames.append(Frame(
194	                index=idx, timestamp=timestamp, src_mac=src_mac,
195	                num_rx=num_rx, num_tx=num_tx, num_subcarriers=num_subcarriers,
196	                rssi1=rssi1, rssi2=rssi2, rate_n_flag=rate_n_flag,
197	                format_code=(rate_n_flag & _RATE_MCS_MOD_TYPE_MSK) >> 8,
198	                width_code=(rate_n_flag & _RATE_MCS_CHAN_WIDTH_MSK) >> 11,
199	                csi_data_size=csi_data_size, csi=csi,
200	            ))
201	            idx += 1
202	    return frames

204	
205	def _stack(frames: list, attr: str) -> np.ndarray:
206	    """
207	    Stack a per-frame complex/real attribute into (F, Rx, Tx, Ns), NaN-padding
208	    the subcarrier/rx/tx axes when frames differ (e.g. channel width changed
209	    mid-capture). Uniform captures stack with no padding.
210	    """
211	    arrays = [getattr(f, attr) if attr != "csi" else f.csi for f in frames]
212	    rx = max(a.shape[0] for a in arrays)
213	    tx = max(a.shape[1] for a in arrays)
214	    ns = max(a.shape[2] for a in arrays)
215	    out = np.full((len(arrays), rx, tx, ns), np.nan, dtype=arrays[0].dtype)
216	    for i, a in enumerate(arrays):
217	        out[i, : a.shape[0], : a.shape[1], : a.shape[2]] = a
218	    return out
219	
220	
221	def drop_pilots(frames: list, verbose: bool = False) -> None:
222	    """Remove pilot subcarriers in-place using the (format, width) tables."""
223	    for f in frames:
224	        # only meaningful when the frame kept its true (rx,tx,ns) shape
225	        ns = f.csi.shape[2]
226	        if ns != f.num_subcarriers:
227	            continue
228	        key = (f.format_name, f.width_mhz)
229	        pilots = _PILOT_INDICES.get(key)
230	        if not pilots:
231	            if verbose:
232	                print(f"  [warn] no pilot table for {key}; frame {f.index} unchanged",
233	                      file=sys.stderr)
234	            continue
235	        keep = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(ns), np.array([p for p in pilots if p < ns]))
236	        f.csi = f.csi[:, :, keep]
237	        f.num_subcarriers = len(keep)
238

240	def write_npz(frames: list, out_path: str) -> None:
241	    magnitude = np.stack([f.magnitude for f in frames]) if _uniform(frames) else _stack(frames, "magnitude")
242	    phase = np.stack([f.phase for f in frames]) if _uniform(frames) else _stack(frames, "phase")
243	    real = _stack(frames, "real") if not _uniform(frames) else np.stack([f.csi.real for f in frames])
244	    imag = _stack(frames, "imag") if not _uniform(frames) else np.stack([f.csi.imag for f in frames])
245	
246	    np.savez_compressed(
247	        out_path,
248	        magnitude=magnitude,
249	        phase=phase,
250	        real=real,
251	        imag=imag,
252	        timestamps=np.array([f.timestamp for f in frames], dtype=np.uint64),
253	        src_mac=np.array([list(f.src_mac) for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
254	        rssi1=np.array([f.rssi1 for f in frames], dtype=np.uint32),
255	        rssi2=np.array([f.rssi2 for f in frames], dtype=np.uint32),
256	        format_code=np.array([f.format_code for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
257	        width_code=np.array([f.width_code for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
258	        num_rx=np.array([f.num_rx for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
259	        num_tx=np.array([f.num_tx for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
260	        num_subcarriers=np.array([f.num_subcarriers for f in frames], dtype=np.uint32),
261	        rate_n_flag=np.array([f.rate_n_flag for f in frames], dtype=np.uint32),
262	    )
263	
264	
265	def _uniform(frames: list) -> bool:
266	    shapes = {f.csi.shape for f in frames}
267	    return len(shapes) == 1

270	def write_csv(frames: list, out_path: str) -> None:
271	    """Tidy long-format CSV: one row per (frame, rx, tx, subcarrier)."""
272	    with open(out_path, "w", newline="") as fh:
273	        w = csv.writer(fh)
274	        w.writerow(["frame", "timestamp", "src_mac", "format", "channel_width_mhz",
275	                    "rssi1", "rssi2", "rx", "tx", "subcarrier",
276	                    "real", "imag", "magnitude", "phase"])
277	        for f in frames:
278	            mag = f.magnitude
279	            pha = f.phase
280	            rx_n, tx_n, ns = f.csi.shape
281	            for r in range(rx_n):
282	                for t in range(tx_n):
283	                    for s in range(ns):
284	                        w.writerow([f.index, f.timestamp, f.src_mac_str,
285	                                    f.format_name, f.width_mhz, f.rssi1, f.rssi2,
286	                                    r, t, s,
287	                                    f"{f.csi[r, t, s].real:.6f}",
288	                                    f"{f.csi[r, t, s].imag:.6f}",
289	                                    f"{mag[r, t, s]:.6f}",
290	                                    f"{pha[r, t, s]:.6f}"])

306	def print_info(frames: list, path: str) -> None:
307	    if not frames:
308	        print(f"{path}: no frames parsed")
309	        return
310	    f0 = frames[0]
311	    macs = sorted({f.src_mac_str for f in frames})
312	    fmts = sorted({(f.format_name, f.width_mhz) for f in frames})
313	    ts = np.array([f.timestamp for f in frames], dtype=np.uint64)
314	    span = (ts[-1] - ts[0]) if len(ts) > 1 else 0
315	    rate = (len(frames) - 1) / (span / 1e6) if span > 0 else float("nan")
316	
317	    print(f"File:            {path}")
318	    print(f"Size:            {os.path.getsize(path)} bytes")
319	    print(f"Frames:          {len(frames)}")
320	    print(f"First frame:     rx={f0.num_rx} tx={f0.num_tx} "
321	          f"subcarriers={f0.num_subcarriers} csiDataSize={f0.csi_data_size}")
322	    print(f"CSI array shape: {f0.csi.shape} (rx, tx, subcarrier)")
323	    print(f"Format(s):       " + ", ".join(f"{n}/{w}MHz" for n, w in fmts))
324	    print(f"Source MAC(s):   " + ", ".join(macs))
325	    print(f"RSSI1 range:     {min(f.rssi1 for f in frames)}..{max(f.rssi1 for f in frames)}")
326	    if span > 0:
327	        print(f"Timestamp span:  {span} (device units)")
328	        print(f"Est. CSI rate:   {rate:.1f} Hz  "
329	              f"(target for falls: 100-1000 Hz)")
330	    uniform = "yes" if _uniform(frames) else "NO (ragged - shapes differ)"
331	    print(f"Uniform shape:   {uniform}")

334	def load_magnitude(path: str) -> np.ndarray:
335	    """Convenience for ML code: return magnitude array shaped (F, Rx, Tx, Ns)."""
336	    frames = parse_dat(path)
337	    if not frames:
338	        raise ValueError(f"no frames in {path}")
339	    if _uniform(frames):
340	        return np.stack([f.magnitude for f in frames])
341	    return _stack(frames, "magnitude")

344	def main(argv=None) -> int:
345	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
346	        description="Parse FeitCSI .dat captures into NumPy/CSV.",
347	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
348	    )
349	    ap.add_argument("input", help="input .dat file")
350	    ap.add_argument("-o", "--output-prefix", default=None,
351	                    help="output filename prefix (default: input basename)")
352	    ap.add_argument("--csv", action="store_true",
353	                    help="also write tidy long-format CSV (can be large)")
354	    ap.add_argument("--meta-csv", action="store_true",
355	                    help="also write per-frame metadata CSV")
356	    ap.add_argument("--drop-pilots", action="store_true",
357	                    help="remove pilot subcarriers using (format,width) tables")
358	    ap.add_argument("--info", action="store_true",
359	                    help="print a summary and exit without writing files")
360	    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
361	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
362

#### Thinking

Bug: In `write_npz` (lines 240–244):

```python
magnitude = np.stack([f.magnitude for f in frames]) if _uniform(frames) else _stack(frames, "magnitude")
phase = np.stack([f.phase for f in frames]) if _uniform(frames) else _stack(frames, "phase")
real = _stack(frames, "real") if not _uniform(frames) else np.stack([f.csi.real for f in frames])
imag = _stack(frames, "imag") if not _uniform(frames) else np.stack([f.csi.imag for f in frames])
```

`_stack(frames, "magnitude")` calls `getattr(f, "magnitude")` — that works (property). `_stack(frames, "real")` calls `getattr(f, "real")` — Frame has no `real` attribute! The Frame dataclass has a `csi` property, plus `magnitude` and `phase` properties, but no `real`/`imag` properties. So in the ragged (non-uniform) path, `_stack(frames, "real")` raises AttributeError.

This bug only surfaces with ragged captures (uniform captures use the `f.csi.real` branch). Our smoke capture was uniform → it worked. This capture is ragged → crash. Exactly as the runbook warned: "the parser was validated with synthetic round-trip tests but has not yet seen a real Zenbook capture."

Fix: add `real` and `imag` properties to Frame:

```python
@property
def real(self) -> np.ndarray:
    return self.csi.real

@property
def imag(self) -> np.ndarray:
    return self.csi.imag
```

This is the minimal, correct fix. Then `_stack(frames, "real")` works.

Note on dtype: `_stack` uses `dtype=arrays[0].dtype` — for real/imag that's float64, and np.full with nan is fine. For magnitude it's float64, phase also float64. Good.

Also check `_stack` for "magnitude": getattr(f, "magnitude") → np.abs(self.csi) works.

One more consideration: for frames stored flat as (1,1,n_samples) (payload mismatch), shape differs — still fine with NaN padding.

9	  Csi::save() opens the file in append mode and writes header+payload per frame,
10	  so records sit back-to-back with no separators.

13	  Payload = csiDataSize/4 complex samples; each sample is 4 bytes:

18	      flat_index = (rx * numTx + tx) * numSubCarriers + subcarrier
19	
20	Header layout (offset, size, field, type):
21	   0   4   csiDataSize     uint32

23	   8   4   ftmClock        uint32

142	def _decode_payload(payload: bytes, num_rx: int, num_tx: int,
143	                    num_subcarriers: int, verbose: bool = False) -> np.ndarray:
144	    """Turn raw payload bytes into a complex array shaped (rx, tx, subcarrier)."""
145	    n_samples = len(payload) // 4
146	    i16 = np.frombuffer(payload[: n_samples * 4], dtype="<i2")
147	    real = i16[0::2].astype(np.float64)
148	    imag = i16[1::2].astype(np.float64)
149	    csi = real + 1j * imag
150	
151	    expected = num_rx * num_tx * num_subcarriers
152	    if expected == n_samples and expected > 0:
153	        return csi.reshape(num_rx, num_tx, num_subcarriers)
154	
155	    if verbose:
156	        print(f"  [warn] payload has {n_samples} samples but header implies "
157	              f"{num_rx}x{num_tx}x{num_subcarriers}={expected}; storing flat",
158	              file=sys.stderr)
159	    return csi.reshape(1, 1, n_samples)

162	def parse_dat(path: str, verbose: bool = False) -> list:
163	    """Read every record in a FeitCSI .dat file. Returns a list of Frame."""
164	    frames = []
165	    size = os.path.getsize(path)
166	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
167	        idx = 0
168	        while True:
169	            header = f.read(CSI_HEADER_LENGTH)
170	            if len(header) == 0:
171	                break  # clean EOF
172	            if len(header) < CSI_HEADER_LENGTH:
173	                print(f"[warn] trailing {len(header)} bytes ignored (partial header)",
174	                      file=sys.stderr)
175	                break
176	
177	            (csi_data_size, _space4, _ftm_clock, timestamp, _space20,
178	             num_rx, num_tx, _space48, num_subcarriers, _space54,
179	             rssi1, rssi2, src_mac, _space75, rate_n_flag, _space96) = _HEADER.unpack(header)
180	
181	            if csi_data_size == 0 or csi_data_size > size:
182	                print(f"[warn] frame {idx}: implausible csiDataSize={csi_data_size}; stopping",
183	                      file=sys.stderr)
184	                break
185	
186	            payload = f.read(csi_data_size)
187	            if len(payload) < csi_data_size:
188	                print(f"[warn] frame {idx}: truncated payload "
189	                      f"({len(payload)}/{csi_data_size}); stopping", file=sys.stderr)
190	                break
191	
192	            csi = _decode_payload(payload, num_rx, num_tx, num_subcarriers, verbose)
193	            frames.append(Frame(
194	                index=idx, timestamp=timestamp, src_mac=src_mac,
195	                num_rx=num_rx, num_tx=num_tx, num_subcarriers=num_subcarriers,
196	                rssi1=rssi1, rssi2=rssi2, rate_n_flag=rate_n_flag,
197	                format_code=(rate_n_flag & _RATE_MCS_MOD_TYPE_MSK) >> 8,
198	                width_code=(rate_n_flag & _RATE_MCS_CHAN_WIDTH_MSK) >> 11,
199	                csi_data_size=csi_data_size, csi=csi,
200	            ))
201	            idx += 1
202	    return frames

205	def _stack(frames: list, attr: str) -> np.ndarray:
206	    """
207	    Stack a per-frame complex/real attribute into (F, Rx, Tx, Ns), NaN-padding
208	    the subcarrier/rx/tx axes when frames differ (e.g. channel width changed
209	    mid-capture). Uniform captures stack with no padding.
210	    """
211	    arrays = [getattr(f, attr) if attr != "csi" else f.csi for f in frames]
212	    rx = max(a.shape[0] for a in arrays)
213	    tx = max(a.shape[1] for a in arrays)
214	    ns = max(a.shape[2] for a in arrays)
215	    out = np.full((len(arrays), rx, tx, ns), np.nan, dtype=arrays[0].dtype)
216	    for i, a in enumerate(arrays):
217	        out[i, : a.shape[0], : a.shape[1], : a.shape[2]] = a
218	    return out

221	def drop_pilots(frames: list, verbose: bool = False) -> None:
222	    """Remove pilot subcarriers in-place using the (format, width) tables."""
223	    for f in frames:
224	        # only meaningful when the frame kept its true (rx,tx,ns) shape
225	        ns = f.csi.shape[2]
226	        if ns != f.num_subcarriers:
227	            continue
228	        key = (f.format_name, f.width_mhz)
229	        pilots = _PILOT_INDICES.get(key)
230	        if not pilots:
231	            if verbose:
232	                print(f"  [warn] no pilot table for {key}; frame {f.index} unchanged",
233	                      file=sys.stderr)
234	            continue
235	        keep = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(ns), np.array([p for p in pilots if p < ns]))
236	        f.csi = f.csi[:, :, keep]
237	        f.num_subcarriers = len(keep)

240	def write_npz(frames: list, out_path: str) -> None:
241	    magnitude = np.stack([f.magnitude for f in frames]) if _uniform(frames) else _stack(frames, "magnitude")
242	    phase = np.stack([f.phase for f in frames]) if _uniform(frames) else _stack(frames, "phase")
243	    real = _stack(frames, "real") if not _uniform(frames) else np.stack([f.csi.real for f in frames])
244	    imag = _stack(frames, "imag") if not _uniform(frames) else np.stack([f.csi.imag for f in frames])
245	
246	    np.savez_compressed(
247	        out_path,
248	        magnitude=magnitude,
249	        phase=phase,
250	        real=real,
251	        imag=imag,
252	        timestamps=np.array([f.timestamp for f in frames], dtype=np.uint64),
253	        src_mac=np.array([list(f.src_mac) for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
254	        rssi1=np.array([f.rssi1 for f in frames], dtype=np.uint32),
255	        rssi2=np.array([f.rssi2 for f in frames], dtype=np.uint32),
256	        format_code=np.array([f.format_code for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
257	        width_code=np.array([f.width_code for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
258	        num_rx=np.array([f.num_rx for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
259	        num_tx=np.array([f.num_tx for f in frames], dtype=np.uint8),
260	        num_subcarriers=np.array([f.num_subcarriers for f in frames], dtype=np.uint32),
261	        rate_n_flag=np.array([f.rate_n_flag for f in frames], dtype=np.uint32),
262	    )
263	
264	
265	def _uniform(frames: list) -> bool:
266	    shapes = {f.csi.shape for f in frames}
267	    return len(shapes) == 1
268	
269	
270	def write_csv(frames: list, out_path: str) -> None:
271	    """Tidy long-format CSV: one row per (frame, rx, tx, subcarrier)."""
272	    with open(out_path, "w", newline="") as fh:
273	        w = csv.writer(fh)
274	        w.writerow(["frame", "timestamp", "src_mac", "format", "channel_width_mhz",
275	                    "rssi1", "rssi2", "rx", "tx", "subcarrier",
276	                    "real", "imag", "magnitude", "phase"])
277	        for f in frames:
278	            mag = f.magnitude
279	            pha = f.phase
280	            rx_n, tx_n, ns = f.csi.shape
281	            for r in range(rx_n):
282	                for t in range(tx_n):
283	                    for s in range(ns):
284	                        w.writerow([f.index, f.timestamp, f.src_mac_str,
285	                                    f.format_name, f.width_mhz, f.rssi1, f.rssi2,
286	                                    r, t, s,
287	                                    f"{f.csi[r, t, s].real:.6f}",
288	                                    f"{f.csi[r, t, s].imag:.6f}",
289	                                    f"{mag[r, t, s]:.6f}",
290	                                    f"{pha[r, t, s]:.6f}"])
291	
292	
293	def write_meta_csv(frames: list, out_path: str) -> None:
294	    """Lightweight per-frame metadata CSV (one row per frame)."""
295	    with open(out_path, "w", newline="") as fh:
296	        w = csv.writer(fh)
297	        w.writerow(["frame", "timestamp", "src_mac", "format", "channel_width_mhz",
298	                    "num_rx", "num_tx", "num_subcarriers", "rssi1", "rssi2",
299	                    "csi_data_size", "rate_n_flag"])
300	        for f in frames:
301	            w.writerow([f.index, f.timestamp, f.src_mac_str, f.format_name,
302	                        f.width_mhz, f.num_rx, f.num_tx, f.num_subcarriers,
303	                        f.rssi1, f.rssi2, f.csi_data_size, f.rate_n_flag])
304

307	    if not frames:

309	        return

329	              f"(target for falls: 100-1000 Hz)")

331	    print(f"Uniform shape:   {uniform}")

**Yes — the MAC filter is implemented**, in three places:

- **CLI `-F xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx`** — parsed at `Arguments.cpp:366-372`
- **GUI field** "Target MAC filter:" — `MainWindow.cpp:96-102`, with format validation and grey-out while measuring
- **Enforcement** — `WiFiCsiController.cpp:105-106`: every CSI frame whose `srcMac` doesn't match is dropped (and freed) before it reaches the output file

This run was **deliberately unfiltered**: the runbook's method is a discovery capture first, because you can't pick a `-F` target until you've seen which MACs are actually on air. Now we know them, so the next capture can be single-device:

```bash
sudo timeout 60 ./bin/app -i measure -f 2412 -w 20 -v -F 22:6e:45:de:34:20 -o /tmp/h3sr_filtered.dat
```

(One caveat: that MAC is a *randomized* client address — it changes when the device reconnects — and bit-flipped header variants won't match an exact filter.)

## Results of the collected data, briefly

- **2736 CSI frames in 60 s ≈ 45 Hz**, all HT/20 MHz, 56 subcarriers, 2 RX chains — passively overheard, zero injection
- **4 real transmitters**: two clients at 44% and 43% (alternating frame-by-frame = both directions of live traffic), a third device at 9%, and H3-SR itself at 1.3%; the long tail of rare MACs are 1–2-bit header errors of those same devices
- **RSSI 65–84**, distinct per transmitter; traffic is bursty (idle gaps visible), which is normal Wi-Fi behavior
- Header timestamps are all zero on this stack, so time = frame index / wall clock

34	int Netlink::nlInit(struct nl80211_state *state)
35	{
36	    int err;
37	    std::string errMsg;
38	
39	    state->nl_sock = nl_socket_alloc();
40	    if (!state->nl_sock)
41	    {
42	        throw std::ios_base::failure("Failed to allocate netlink socket.\n");
43	        return -ENOMEM;
44	    }
45	
46	    if (genl_connect(state->nl_sock))
47	    {
48	        errMsg = "Failed to connect to generic netlink.\n";
49	        err = -ENOLINK;
50	        goto out_handle_destroy;
51	    }
52	
53	    nl_socket_set_buffer_size(state->nl_sock, 8192, 8192);
54	
55	    /* try to set NETLINK_EXT_ACK to 1, ignoring errors */
56	    err = 1;
57	    setsockopt(nl_socket_get_fd(state->nl_sock), SOL_NETLINK,
58	               NETLINK_EXT_ACK, &err, sizeof(err));
59	
60	    state->nl80211_id = genl_ctrl_resolve(state->nl_sock, "nl80211");
61	
62	    if (state->nl80211_id < 0)
63	    {
64	        errMsg = "nl80211 not found.\n";
65	        err = -ENOENT;
66	        goto out_handle_destroy;
67	    }
68	
69	    return 0;
70	
71	out_handle_destroy:
72	    nl_socket_free(state->nl_sock);
73	    if (!errMsg.empty())
74	    {
75	        throw std::ios_base::failure(errMsg);
76	    }
77	    
78	    return err;
79	}
80	
81	int Netlink::nlExecCommand(Cmd &cmd)
82	{
83	    int err = 0;
84	    std::string errMsg;
85	    struct nl_msg *msg = nlmsg_alloc();
86	    if (!msg)
87	    {
88	        throw std::ios_base::failure("failed to allocate netlink message\n");
89	        return 2;
90	    }
91	
92	    struct nl_cb *cb = nl_cb_alloc(NL_CB_DEFAULT);
93	    struct nl_cb *s_cb = nl_cb_alloc(NL_CB_DEFAULT);
94	
95	    if (!cb || !s_cb)
96	    {
97	        errMsg = "failed to allocate netlink callbacks\n";
98	        err = 2;
99	        goto out;
100	    }
101	
102	    genlmsg_put(msg, 0, 0, this->nlstate.nl80211_id, 0, cmd.nlFlags, cmd.id, 0);
103	
104	    switch (cmd.idby)
105	    {
106	    case CIB_PHY:
107	        NLA_PUT_U32(msg, NL80211_ATTR_WIPHY, cmd.device);
108	        break;
109	    case CIB_NETDEV:
110	        NLA_PUT_U32(msg, NL80211_ATTR_IFINDEX, cmd.device);
111	        break;
112	    case CIB_WDEV:
113	        NLA_PUT_U64(msg, NL80211_ATTR_WDEV, cmd.device);
114	        break;
115	    default:
116	        break;
117	    }
118	
119	    if (cmd.handler)
120	    {
121	        err = cmd.handler(&this->nlstate, msg, cmd.args);
122	    }
123	
124	    if (err)
125	        goto out;
126	
127	    nl_socket_set_cb(this->nlstate.nl_sock, s_cb);
128	
129	    err = nl_send_auto_complete(this->nlstate.nl_sock, msg);
130	    
131	    if (err < 0)
132	        goto out;
133	
134	    err = 1;
135	
136	    nl_cb_err(cb, NL_CB_CUSTOM, this->error_handler, &err);
137	    nl_cb_set(cb, NL_CB_FINISH, NL_CB_CUSTOM, this->finish_handler, &err);
138	    nl_cb_set(cb, NL_CB_ACK, NL_CB_CUSTOM, this->ack_handler, &err);
139	    nl_cb_set(cb, NL_CB_MSG_IN, NL_CB_CUSTOM, cmd.valid_handler ? cmd.valid_handler : this->nlValidHandler, this);
140	    while (err > 0)
141	    {
142	        nl_recvmsgs(this->nlstate.nl_sock, cb);
143	    }
144	
145	    if (err < 0)
146	    {
147	        errMsg = "command failed: " + std::string(strerror(-err)) + std::to_string(err) + "\n";
148	    }
149	out:
150	    nl_cb_put(cb);
151	    nl_cb_put(s_cb);
152	    nlmsg_free(msg);
153	    if (!errMsg.empty())
154	    {
155	        throw std::ios_base::failure(errMsg);
156	    }
157	    return err;
158	nla_put_failure:
159	    throw std::ios_base::failure("building message failed\n");
160	    return 2;
161	}

168	int Netlink::error_handler(struct sockaddr_nl *nla, struct nlmsgerr *err, void *arg)
169	{
170	    struct nlmsghdr *nlh = (struct nlmsghdr *)err - 1;
171	    int len = nlh->nlmsg_len;
172	    struct nlattr *attrs;
173	    struct nlattr *tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MAX + 1];
174	    int *ret = (int *)arg;
175	    int ack_len = sizeof(*nlh) + sizeof(int) + sizeof(*nlh);
176	
177	    if (err->error > 0)
178	    {
179	        /*
180	         * This is illegal, per netlink(7), but not impossible (think
181	         * "vendor commands"). Callers really expect negative error
182	         * codes, so make that happen.
183	         */
184	
185	        throw std::ios_base::failure("ERROR: received positive netlink error code " + std::to_string(err->error) + "\n");
186	        *ret = -EPROTO;
187	    }
188	    else
189	    {
190	        *ret = err->error;
191	    }
192	
193	    if (!(nlh->nlmsg_flags & NLM_F_ACK_TLVS))
194	        return NL_STOP;
195	
196	    if (!(nlh->nlmsg_flags & NLM_F_CAPPED))
197	        ack_len += err->msg.nlmsg_len - sizeof(*nlh);
198	
199	    if (len <= ack_len)
200	        return NL_STOP;
201	
202	    attrs = (nlattr *)((unsigned char *)nlh + ack_len);
203	    len -= ack_len;
204	
205	    nla_parse(tb, NLMSGERR_ATTR_MAX, attrs, len, NULL);
206	    if (tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG])
207	    {
208	        len = strnlen((char *)nla_data(tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG]),
209	                      nla_len(tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG]));
210	
211	        throw std::ios_base::failure("kernel reports: " + std::string((char *)nla_data(tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG])) + "\n");
212	    }
213	
214	    return NL_STOP;
215	}

#### Thinking

The nl plumbing supports dumps: `Cmd.nlFlags` is passed to genlmsg_put as flags — for a dump request we need NLM_F_DUMP in the nlmsg flags. genlmsg_put(msg, port, seq, family, hdrlen, flags, cmd, version) — the `flags` parameter goes into nlh->nlmsg_flags. So Cmd{.id=NL80211_CMD_GET_SCAN, .idby=CIB_PHY or CIB_NETDEV, .nlFlags=NLM_F_DUMP, .valid_handler=scanHandler} works: the receive loop continues until NL_CB_FINISH (dump sends NLMSG_DONE → finish_handler sets err=0). The valid_handler is called for each message (NL_CB_MSG_IN) — that's where we parse each BSS entry.

Note: nl_cb_set(cb, NL_CB_MSG_IN, ..., cmd.valid_handler ? ... : nlValidHandler, this) — arg passed to valid_handler is `this` (Netlink*), not cmd.args! Look: line 139: `nl_cb_set(cb, NL_CB_MSG_IN, NL_CB_CUSTOM, cmd.valid_handler ? cmd.valid_handler : this->nlValidHandler, this);` — arg = `this`. Hmm, so the handler receives the Netlink instance as arg, not cmd.args. But existing handlers like processGetInterfacesHandler are static and take (nl_msg*, void* arg)... how do they get cmd.args? They don't via this path... wait, but cmd.handler (the pre-send handler) takes (state, msg, arg=cmd.args). The valid_handler (receive side) takes (msg, this). So receive-side handlers can't access cmd.args directly... but they're static member functions of WiFIController — `this` is a Netlink*, not a WiFIController*... hmm, WiFIController inherits from Netlink; static handlers cast arg? Let me check processGetInterfacesHandler in WiFIController.cpp to see the pattern.

505	    unsigned int cf1 = freq, j;
506	    unsigned int bw80[] = {5180, 5260, 5500, 5580, 5660, 5745,

514

518	        /* setup center_freq1 */

520	        {
521	            if (freq >= bw80[j] && freq < bw80[j] + 80)
522	                break;
523	        }
524	
525	        if (j == ARRAY_SIZE(bw80))
526	            break;
527

530	    case NL80211_CHAN_WIDTH_160:
531	        /* setup center_freq1 */

533	        {
534	            if (freq >= bw160[j] && freq < bw160[j] + 160)
535	                break;
536	        }
537	
538	        if (j == ARRAY_SIZE(bw160))
539	            break;
540	
541	        cf1 = bw160[j] + 70;
542	        break;
543	    case NL80211_CHAN_WIDTH_320:
544	        /* setup center_freq1 */
545	        for (j = 0; j < ARRAY_SIZE(bw320); j++)
546	        {
547	            if (freq >= bw320[j] && freq < bw320[j] + 160)

43	gint MainController::updatePlots()
44	{
45	    std::vector<Csi *> batch;
46	
47	    WiFiCsiController::csiQueueMutex.lock();
48	    while (!WiFiCsiController::csiQueue.empty())
49	    {
50	        batch.push_back(WiFiCsiController::csiQueue.front());
51	        WiFiCsiController::csiQueue.pop();
52	    }
53	    WiFiCsiController::csiQueueMutex.unlock();
54	
55	    if (batch.empty())
56	    {
57	        return (TRUE);
58	    }
59	
60	    MainController *mainController = MainController::getInstance();
61	
62	    // Every captured frame becomes a row in the waterfall.
63	    if (mainController->waterfall)
64	    {
65	        for (Csi *c : batch)
66	        {
67	            mainController->waterfall->addFrame(c->magnitude, c->numSubCarriers);
68	        }
69	    }
70	
71	    // The newest frame drives the amplitude/phase line plots; free the rest.
72	    if (csiToPlot)
73	    {
74	        delete csiToPlot;
75	    }
76	    csiToPlot = batch.back();
77	    for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < batch.size(); i++)
78	    {
79	        delete batch[i];
80	    }
81	
82	    mainController->plotAmplitude->updateData(csiToPlot, &csiToPlot->magnitude);
83	    mainController->plotPhase->updateData(csiToPlot, &csiToPlot->phase);
84	
85	    return (TRUE);
86	}

88	gint MainController::updateStatus()
89	{
90	    MainController *mainController = MainController::getInstance();
91	    if (!mainController->statusLight)
92	    {
93	        return TRUE;
94	    }
95	
96	    const int64_t now = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
97	                            std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
98	                            .count();
99	    const int64_t threshold = 1000;
100	    const int64_t accepted = MainController::lastAcceptedMs.load();
101	    const int64_t any = MainController::lastAnyCsiMs.load();
102	
103	    StatusLight::State state;
104	    std::string text;
105	
106	    if (MainController::captureError.load())
107	    {
108	        state = StatusLight::ERR;
109	        text = "Error - capture failed (NIC/driver)";
110	    }
111	    else if (!MainController::measuringActive.load())
112	    {
113	        state = StatusLight::IDLE;
114	        text = "Idle - not measuring";
115	    }
116	    else if (accepted != 0 && now - accepted < threshold)
117	    {
118	        state = StatusLight::OK;
119	        text = "Capturing target-device CSI";
120	    }
121	    else if (any != 0 && now - any < threshold)
122	    {
123	        state = StatusLight::WARN;
124	        text = "CSI seen - no frames match target filter";
125	    }
126	    else
127	    {
128	        state = StatusLight::ERR;
129	        text = "No CSI - check channel/NIC/transmitter";
130	    }
131	
132	    mainController->statusLight->setState(state, text);
133	    return TRUE;
134	}

392	void *MainController::ftm(void *arg)
393	{
394	    bool firstRun = true;
395	    try
396	    {
397	        MainController::getInstance()->wifiController.setInterfaceUpDown(AP_INTERFACE_NAME, true);
398	        WiFiFtmController wft;
399	        wft.init();
400	        if (Arguments::arguments.measure)
401	        {
402	            uint64_t startFtmTime = 0;
403	            while (1)
404	            {
405	                std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(Arguments::arguments.injectDelay));
406	                try
407	                {
408	                    wft.startInitiator();
409	                }
410	                catch(const std::exception& e)
411	                {
412	                    std::cerr << e.what() << '\n';
413	                }
414	                
415	                
416	                if (wft.lastRttIsSuccess && firstRun)
417	                {
418	                    firstRun = false;
419	                    startFtmTime = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();
420	                }
421	
422	                uint64_t now = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();
423	                if ((startFtmTime + (Arguments::arguments.modeDelay / 2)) > now)
424	                {
425	                    continue;
426	                }
427	
428	                if (!wft.lastRttIsSuccess && !firstRun)
429	                {
430	                    MainController::getInstance()->measureCsi(false);
431	                    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(Arguments::arguments.modeDelay));
432	                    MainController::getInstance()->measureCsi(true);
433	                    WiFiCsiController::enableCsi(false);
434	                    firstRun = true;
435	                    MainController::getInstance()->wifiController.setInterfaceUpDown(MONITOR_INTERFACE_NAME, false);
436	                    MainController::getInstance()->wifiController.setInterfaceUpDown(AP_INTERFACE_NAME, true);
437	                }
438	            }
439	        }
440	        else
441	        {
442	            if (Arguments::arguments.injectRepeat)
443	            {
444	                for (uint32_t i = 0; i < Arguments::arguments.injectRepeat; i++)
445	                {
446	                    wft.startInitiator();
447	                    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(Arguments::arguments.injectDelay));
448	                }
449	            }
450	            else
451	            {
452	                while (true)
453	                {
454	                    wft.startInitiator();
455	                    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::microseconds(Arguments::arguments.injectDelay));
456	                }
457	            }
458	        }
459	    }
460	    catch (const std::exception &e)
461	    {
462	        if (MainController::mainWindow)
463	        {
464	            MainController::mainWindow->fatalError(e.what());
465	        }
466	        else
467	        {
468	            Logger::log(error) << e.what() << '\n';
469	        }
470	    }
471	
472	    return 0;
473	}

583	void MainController::restoreState()
584	{
585	    MainController *mainController = MainController::getInstance();
586	
587	    if (mainController->measureCsiThread)
588	    {
589	        pthread_cancel(mainController->measureCsiThread);
590	    }
591	    if (mainController->injectPacketThread)
592	    {
593	        pthread_cancel(mainController->injectPacketThread);
594	    }
595	
596	    mainController->wifiController.removeInterface(MONITOR_INTERFACE_NAME);
597	    mainController->wifiController.removeInterface(AP_INTERFACE_NAME);
598	    for (InterfaceInfo interface : mainController->bkpInterfaces)
599	    {
600	        if (Arguments::arguments.verbose)
601	        {
602	            Logger::log(info) << "Recovering interface " << interface.ifName << "\n";
603	        }
604	        mainController->wifiController.addDevice(interface.ifName.c_str(), (nl80211_iftype)interface.ifType);
605	    }
606	    mainController->bkpInterfaces.clear();
607	    mainController->wifiController.interfaces.clear();
608	
609	    if (Arguments::arguments.verbose)
610	    {
611	        Logger::log(info) << "Exiting recovery state...\n";
612	    }
613	}

#### Thinking

Key insight: `MainController::initInterface()` is where the interfaces get destroyed — this is called at the start of runNoGui/runGui. The Wi-Fi picker menu must run **before** initInterface() (while the original interfaces still exist and the kernel's scan cache is fresh / triggering a scan is possible).

Best insertion point: inside `main.cpp`, after argument parsing, before MainController's execution — or at the top of runNoGui/runGui, before initInterface(). However, scanning requires a netlink socket + an interface index for triggering. WiFIController has init() (Netlink::init). We can create a temporary WiFIController inside main.cpp before dispatch: scan, display menu, set args. But WiFIController::init() just initializes netlink. Scanning requires an ifindex or wiphy for TRIGGER_SCAN. GET_SCAN dump can be done with CIB_NONE? A GET_SCAN dump without wiphy/ifindex dumps all — actually, a GET_SCAN dump requires either wiphy or ifindex? In iw: `iw dev <dev> scan dump` uses ifindex; `iw phy <phy> scan dump`? Hmm, kernel: NL80211_CMD_GET_SCAN dump — requires wiphy or netdev? Looking at nl80211: the get_scan dump handler uses the request's wiphy... in iw's scan dump: handle_scan_dump uses CIB_PHY or CIB_NETDEV? iw's scan dump: `__scan_trigger`... in iw.c, the scan dump command is defined with CIB_PHY and CIB_NETDEV variants? iw's scan.c: COMMAND(scan, dump, ..., NL80211_CMD_GET_SCAN, NLM_F_DUMP, ...) is registered for both CIB_PHY and CIB_NETDEV. The kernel's nl80211_get_scan_dump uses the wiphy from get_rdev_dev(...)... it accepts either.

Simplest: use CIB_NETDEV with the ifindex of the first existing wireless interface (from getInterfaces()). But getInterfaces() lists all interfaces including non-wireless? It dumps NL80211 interfaces (wireless only). Good: WiFIController::getInterfaces() fills the interfaces vector; pick interfaces[0].ifIndex.

Flow of the CLI menu (before initInterface):
1. WiFIController wc; wc.init(); wc.getInterfaces();
2. If interfaces is empty → skip the menu.
3. wc.triggerScan(ifindex); sleep ~2.5s; wc.scanNetworks(ifindex) → vector<ScanResult>.
   - TRIGGER_SCAN may fail (EBUSY if NM is scanning) — ignore the error and use the cached dump.
4. Display list; read selection from stdin; set Arguments::arguments.frequency = sel.freq; filterMac = sel.bssid; filterMacEnabled = true.
5. Continue to normal flow.

But note: WiFIController's instance inside main vs. MainController's wifiController member — separate instances, no problem (netlink sockets are independent).

Where to put the menu code? A new small module, or inside WiFIController + a function in main.cpp. Cleaner: add to WiFIController: `std::vector<ScanResult> scanNetworks(int ifIndex)` and `void triggerScan(int ifIndex)`. And a free function for the CLI menu in main.cpp (or MainController::runNoGui before initInterface? runNoGui is also called from GUI? No — runGui is separate. But the CLI menu should only run in non-GUI mode and when stdin is a TTY and the mode includes measure).

Hmm, wait — the GUI also needs scanning (the dialog). The GUI dialog calls wc.scanNetworks() directly. Good: the scan function is shared; the menu UI differs.

Placement of the CLI menu call: at the top of MainController::runNoGui(), before initInterface(), gated by: !gui (runNoGui implies that), Arguments::arguments.measure, isatty(STDIN_FILENO). But runNoGui is also used in UDP mode? runUdpSocket is separate. OK.

Hmm — but runNoGui(bool detach) might be called from elsewhere? Only from main.cpp. No problem.

Alternatively, put the menu in main.cpp before dispatch — but then it would also run in -u udp mode... gate by measure. I'll put it at the top of runNoGui.

GUI: MainWindow — need to look at its header/cpp to add a button + dialog. The GUI is built from a glade string (layout.h — generated?). MainWindow.glade → embedded in layout.h. Adding widgets: MainWindow.cpp programmatically creates some widgets (the filterMac entry was added in code at row 18 of settingsGrid). So we can add a "Wi-Fi…" button in code next to it. Dialog: build programmatically (Gtk::Dialog with a TreeView or ListBox). Programmatic = no glade editing.

Scan in GUI: on button click → run triggerScan+dump synchronously (UI freezes for ~2-3s; acceptable? Better UX: display the dialog with a "Scanning…" label, run the scan via Glib::Threads? Complexity. For an FYP tool, a synchronous scan with a wait cursor is acceptable; NM is still running at that point (the GUI kills NM only when measurement starts). Actually, triggerScan while NM is managing: the kernel allows concurrent scan requests. Then the dump returns a mix of old+new; filter by seen_ms_ago? Keep everything and sort by signal.

Simplification: don't trigger a scan at all — just dump the kernel/NM scan cache (NM scans periodically every ~30s when connected, less often when disconnected... when disconnected NM scans periodically too). Risk: stale/empty cache on first use. Compromise: try triggerScan, catch exceptions, sleep 2s, then dump. In GUI, do this synchronously inside the dialog's constructor with a "Scanning..." spinner text — 2s freeze is OK.

Security detection for the lock icon: parse IEs for RSN (id 48) or WPA vendor IE (0xdd with OUI 00:50:f2:01) → secured. Simple: if either is present, secured=true.

SSID from IE 0 inside NL80211_BSS_INFORMATION_ELEMENTS. Hidden SSIDs (length 0) → display BSSID instead.

Signal: NL80211_BSS_SIGNAL_MBM (u32, signed value in mbm) → dBm = mbm/100. Some drivers give NL80211_BSS_SIGNAL_UNSPEC (0-100). Handle both.

Frequency: NL80211_BSS_FREQUENCY (u32 MHz).

Deduplication: multiple BSS entries per SSID (one per BSSID) is fine — list them all; also dedupe identical (ssid,bssid)? The kernel usually returns one entry per BSSID.

Sort: by signal descending.

775	int WiFIController::freqToCHannel(int freq)
776	{
777	    if (freq < 1000)
778	        return 0;
779	    /* see 802.11-2007 17.3.8.3.2 and Annex J */
780	    if (freq == 2484)
781	        return 14;
782	    /* see 802.11ax D6.1 27.3.23.2 and Annex E */
783	    else if (freq == 5935)
784	        return 2;
785	    else if (freq < 2484)
786	        return (freq - 2407) / 5;
787	    else if (freq >= 4910 && freq <= 4980)
788	        return (freq - 4000) / 5;
789	    else if (freq < 5950)
790	        return (freq - 5000) / 5;
791	    else if (freq <= 45000) /* DMG band lower limit */
792	        /* see 802.11ax D6.1 27.3.23.2 */
793	        return (freq - 5950) / 5;
794	    else if (freq >= 58320 && freq <= 70200)
795	        return (freq - 56160) / 2160;
796	    else
797	        return 0;
798	}

```cpp
void WiFIController::triggerScan(int ifIndex)
{
    Cmd cmd{
        .id = NL80211_CMD_TRIGGER_SCAN,
        .idby = CIB_NETDEV,
        .nlFlags = 0,
        .device = ifIndex,
        .handler = NULL,
        .valid_handler = NULL,
    };

}
```

Wait — Cmd struct field order. Let me check the Cmd struct definition to ensure designated initializer order matches. The order in the struct is: id, idby, nlFlags, device, handler, valid_handler, args. In getInterfaces they used id, idby, nlFlags, handler, valid_handler (skipping device). Designated initializers in C++ must be in declaration order, and you can skip. So id, idby, nlFlags, device, handler, valid_handler is fine.

```cpp
std::vector<ScanResult> WiFIController::scanNetworks(int ifIndex)
{
    this->scanResults.clear();

    try
    {
        this->triggerScan(ifIndex);
    }
    catch (const std::exception &e)
    {
        // Another process (e.g. NetworkManager) may hold the scan lock.
        // Fall through to dump whatever cached results the kernel has.
        if (Arguments::arguments.verbose)
        {
            Logger::log(warning) << "Scan trigger failed, using cached results: " << e.what() << "\n";
        }
    }

    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(2000));

    Cmd cmd{
        .id = NL80211_CMD_GET_SCAN,
        .idby = CIB_NETDEV,
        .nlFlags = NLM_F_DUMP,
        .device = ifIndex,
        .handler = NULL,
        .valid_handler = this->processGetScanHandler,
    };
    this->nlExecCommand(cmd);

    std::stable_sort(this->scanResults.begin(), this->scanResults.end(),
                     [](const ScanResult &a, const ScanResult &b)
                     { return a.signalDbm > b.signalDbm; });

    return this->scanResults;
}
```

```cpp
int WiFIController::processGetScanHandler(struct nl_msg *msg, void *arg)
{
    WiFIController *instance = (WiFIController *)arg;
    struct genlmsghdr *gnlh = (genlmsghdr *)nlmsg_data(nlmsg_hdr(msg));
    struct nlattr *tb_msg[NL80211_ATTR_MAX + 1];
    struct nlattr *tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_MAX + 1];

    nla_parse(tb_msg, NL80211_ATTR_MAX, genlmsg_attrdata(gnlh, 0),
              genlmsg_attrlen(gnlh, 0), NULL);

    if (!tb_msg[NL80211_ATTR_BSS])
    {
        return NL_SKIP;
    }

    nla_parse_nested(tb_bss, NL80211_BSS_MAX, tb_msg[NL80211_ATTR_BSS], NULL);

    ScanResult result;
    bool haveBssid = false;

    if (tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_BSSID])
    {
        result.bssid = instance->macN2a((const unsigned char *)nla_data(tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_BSSID]));
        haveBssid = true;
    }
    if (tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_FREQUENCY])
    {
        result.freq = nla_get_u32(tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_FREQUENCY]);
        result.channel = WiFIController::frequencyToChannel(result.freq);
    }
    if (tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_SIGNAL_MBM])
    {
        result.signalDbm = (int)nla_get_u32(tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_SIGNAL_MBM]) / 100;
    }
    else if (tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_SIGNAL_UNSPEC])
    {
        result.signalDbm = (int)nla_get_u8(tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_SIGNAL_UNSPEC]);
    }

    if (tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_INFORMATION_ELEMENTS])
    {
        // parse IEs
        unsigned char *ies = (unsigned char *)nla_data(tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_INFORMATION_ELEMENTS]);
        int len = nla_len(tb_bss[NL80211_BSS_INFORMATION_ELEMENTS]);
        int i = 0;
        while (i + 1 < len)
        {
            uint8_t id = ies[i];
            uint8_t elen = ies[i + 1];
            if (i + 2 + elen > len) break;
            unsigned char *data = ies + i + 2;
            if (id == 0) // SSID
            {
                result.ssid = std::string((const char *)data, elen);
            }
            else if (id == 48) // RSN
            {
                result.secured = true;
            }
            else if (id == 221 && elen >= 4 &&
                     data[0] == 0x00 && data[1] == 0x50 && data[2] == 0xf2 && data[3] == 0x01) // WPA
            {
                result.secured = true;
            }
            i += 2 + elen;
        }
    }

    if (!haveBssid)
    {
        return NL_SKIP;
    }
    if (result.ssid.empty())
    {
        result.ssid = "<hidden " + result.bssid + ">";
    }

    instance->scanResults.push_back(result);
    return NL_OK;
}
```

34	int Netlink::nlInit(struct nl80211_state *state)
35	{
36	    int err;
37	    std::string errMsg;
38	
39	    state->nl_sock = nl_socket_alloc();
40	    if (!state->nl_sock)
41	    {
42	        throw std::ios_base::failure("Failed to allocate netlink socket.\n");
43	        return -ENOMEM;
44	    }
45	
46	    if (genl_connect(state->nl_sock))
47	    {
48	        errMsg = "Failed to connect to generic netlink.\n";
49	        err = -ENOLINK;
50	        goto out_handle_destroy;
51	    }
52	
53	    nl_socket_set_buffer_size(state->nl_sock, 8192, 8192);
54	
55	    /* try to set NETLINK_EXT_ACK to 1, ignoring errors */
56	    err = 1;
57	    setsockopt(nl_socket_get_fd(state->nl_sock), SOL_NETLINK,
58	               NETLINK_EXT_ACK, &err, sizeof(err));
59	
60	    state->nl80211_id = genl_ctrl_resolve(state->nl_sock, "nl80211");
61	
62	    if (state->nl80211_id < 0)
63	    {
64	        errMsg = "nl80211 not found.\n";
65	        err = -ENOENT;
66	        goto out_handle_destroy;
67	    }
68	
69	    return 0;
70	
71	out_handle_destroy:
72	    nl_socket_free(state->nl_sock);
73	    if (!errMsg.empty())
74	    {
75	        throw std::ios_base::failure(errMsg);
76	    }
77	    
78	    return err;
79	}

81	int Netlink::nlExecCommand(Cmd &cmd)
82	{
83	    int err = 0;
84	    std::string errMsg;
85	    struct nl_msg *msg = nlmsg_alloc();
86	    if (!msg)
87	    {
88	        throw std::ios_base::failure("failed to allocate netlink message\n");
89	        return 2;
90	    }
91	
92	    struct nl_cb *cb = nl_cb_alloc(NL_CB_DEFAULT);
93	    struct nl_cb *s_cb = nl_cb_alloc(NL_CB_DEFAULT);
94	
95	    if (!cb || !s_cb)
96	    {
97	        errMsg = "failed to allocate netlink callbacks\n";
98	        err = 2;
99	        goto out;
100	    }
101	
102	    genlmsg_put(msg, 0, 0, this->nlstate.nl80211_id, 0, cmd.nlFlags, cmd.id, 0);
103	
104	    switch (cmd.idby)
105	    {
106	    case CIB_PHY:
107	        NLA_PUT_U32(msg, NL80211_ATTR_WIPHY, cmd.device);
108	        break;
109	    case CIB_NETDEV:
110	        NLA_PUT_U32(msg, NL80211_ATTR_IFINDEX, cmd.device);
111	        break;
112	    case CIB_WDEV:
113	        NLA_PUT_U64(msg, NL80211_ATTR_WDEV, cmd.device);
114	        break;
115	    default:
116	        break;
117	    }
118	
119	    if (cmd.handler)
120	    {
121	        err = cmd.handler(&this->nlstate, msg, cmd.args);
122	    }
123	
124	    if (err)
125	        goto out;
126	
127	    nl_socket_set_cb(this->nlstate.nl_sock, s_cb);
128	
129	    err = nl_send_auto_complete(this->nlstate.nl_sock, msg);
130	    
131	    if (err < 0)
132	        goto out;
133	
134	    err = 1;
135	
136	    nl_cb_err(cb, NL_CB_CUSTOM, this->error_handler, &err);
137	    nl_cb_set(cb, NL_CB_FINISH, NL_CB_CUSTOM, this->finish_handler, &err);
138	    nl_cb_set(cb, NL_CB_ACK, NL_CB_CUSTOM, this->ack_handler, &err);
139	    nl_cb_set(cb, NL_CB_MSG_IN, NL_CB_CUSTOM, cmd.valid_handler ? cmd.valid_handler : this->nlValidHandler, this);
140	    while (err > 0)
141	    {
142	        nl_recvmsgs(this->nlstate.nl_sock, cb);
143	    }
144	
145	    if (err < 0)
146	    {
147	        errMsg = "command failed: " + std::string(strerror(-err)) + std::to_string(err) + "\n";
148	    }
149	out:
150	    nl_cb_put(cb);
151	    nl_cb_put(s_cb);
152	    nlmsg_free(msg);
153	    if (!errMsg.empty())
154	    {
155	        throw std::ios_base::failure(errMsg);
156	    }
157	    return err;
158	nla_put_failure:
159	    throw std::ios_base::failure("building message failed\n");
160	    return 2;
161	}

168	int Netlink::error_handler(struct sockaddr_nl *nla, struct nlmsgerr *err, void *arg)
169	{
170	    struct nlmsghdr *nlh = (struct nlmsghdr *)err - 1;
171	    int len = nlh->nlmsg_len;
172	    struct nlattr *attrs;
173	    struct nlattr *tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MAX + 1];
174	    int *ret = (int *)arg;
175	    int ack_len = sizeof(*nlh) + sizeof(int) + sizeof(*nlh);
176	
177	    if (err->error > 0)
178	    {
179	        /*
180	         * This is illegal, per netlink(7), but not impossible (think
181	         * "vendor commands"). Callers really expect negative error
182	         * codes, so make that happen.
183	         */
184	
185	        throw std::ios_base::failure("ERROR: received positive netlink error code " + std::to_string(err->error) + "\n");
186	        *ret = -EPROTO;
187	    }
188	    else
189	    {
190	        *ret = err->error;
191	    }
192	
193	    if (!(nlh->nlmsg_flags & NLM_F_ACK_TLVS))
194	        return NL_STOP;
195	
196	    if (!(nlh->nlmsg_flags & NLM_F_CAPPED))
197	        ack_len += err->msg.nlmsg_len - sizeof(*nlh);
198	
199	    if (len <= ack_len)
200	        return NL_STOP;
201	
202	    attrs = (nlattr *)((unsigned char *)nlh + ack_len);
203	    len -= ack_len;
204	
205	    nla_parse(tb, NLMSGERR_ATTR_MAX, attrs, len, NULL);
206	    if (tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG])
207	    {
208	        len = strnlen((char *)nla_data(tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG]),
209	                      nla_len(tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG]));
210	
211	        throw std::ios_base::failure("kernel reports: " + std::string((char *)nla_data(tb[NLMSGERR_ATTR_MSG])) + "\n");
212	    }
213	
214	    return NL_STOP;
215	}

503	int WiFIController::getCf1(const struct ChanMode *chanmode, unsigned long freq)
504	{
505	    unsigned int cf1 = freq, j;
506	    unsigned int bw80[] = {5180, 5260, 5500, 5580, 5660, 5745,
507	                           5955, 6035, 6115, 6195, 6275, 6355,
508	                           6435, 6515, 6595, 6675, 6755, 6835,
509	                           6195, 6995};
510	    unsigned int bw160[] = {5180, 5500, 5955, 6115, 6275, 6435,
511	                            6595, 6755, 6915};
512	    /* based on 11be D2 E.1 Country information and operating classes */
513	    unsigned int bw320[] = {5955, 6115, 6275, 6435, 6595, 6755};
514	
515	    switch (chanmode->width)
516	    {
517	    case NL80211_CHAN_WIDTH_80:
518	        /* setup center_freq1 */
519	        for (j = 0; j < ARRAY_SIZE(bw80); j++)
520	        {
521	            if (freq >= bw80[j] && freq < bw80[j] + 80)
522	                break;
523	        }
524	
525	        if (j == ARRAY_SIZE(bw80))
526	            break;
527	
528	        cf1 = bw80[j] + 30;
529	        break;
530	    case NL80211_CHAN_WIDTH_160:
531	        /* setup center_freq1 */
532	        for (j = 0; j < ARRAY_SIZE(bw160); j++)
533	        {
534	            if (freq >= bw160[j] && freq < bw160[j] + 160)
535	                break;
536	        }
537	
538	        if (j == ARRAY_SIZE(bw160))
539	            break;
540	
541	        cf1 = bw160[j] + 70;
542	        break;
543	    case NL80211_CHAN_WIDTH_320:
544	        /* setup center_freq1 */
545	        for (j = 0; j < ARRAY_SIZE(bw320); j++)
546	        {
547	            if (freq >= bw320[j] && freq < bw320[j] + 160)
548	                break;
549	        }
550	
551	        if (j == ARRAY_SIZE(bw320))
552	            break;
553	
554	        cf1 = bw320[j] + 150;
555	        break;
556	    default:
557	        cf1 = freq + chanmode->freq1_diff;
558	        break;
559	    }
560	
561	    return cf1;
562	}

43	gint MainController::updatePlots()
44	{
45	    std::vector<Csi *> batch;
46	
47	    WiFiCsiController::csiQueueMutex.lock();
48	    while (!WiFiCsiController::csiQueue.empty())
49	    {
50	        batch.push_back(WiFiCsiController::csiQueue.front());
51	        WiFiCsiController::csiQueue.pop();
52	    }
53	    WiFiCsiController::csiQueueMutex.unlock();
54	
55	    if (batch.empty())
56	    {
57	        return (TRUE);
58	    }
59	
60	    MainController *mainController = MainController::getInstance();
61	
62	    // Every captured frame becomes a row in the waterfall.
63	    if (mainController->waterfall)
64	    {
65	        for (Csi *c : batch)
66	        {
67	            mainController->waterfall->addFrame(c->magnitude, c->numSubCarriers);
68	        }
69	    }
70	
71	    // The newest frame drives the amplitude/phase line plots; free the rest.
72	    if (csiToPlot)
73	    {
74	        delete csiToPlot;
75	    }
76	    csiToPlot = batch.back();
77	    for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < batch.size(); i++)
78	    {
79	        delete batch[i];
80	    }
81	
82	    mainController->plotAmplitude->updateData(csiToPlot, &csiToPlot->magnitude);
83	    mainController->plotPhase->updateData(csiToPlot, &csiToPlot->phase);
84	
85	    return (TRUE);
86	}

88	gint MainController::updateStatus()
89	{
90	    MainController *mainController = MainController::getInstance();
91	    if (!mainController->statusLight)
92	    {
93	        return TRUE;
94	    }
95	
96	    const int64_t now = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
97	                            std::chrono::system_clock::now().time_since_epoch())
98	                            .count();
99	    const int64_t threshold = 1000;
100	    const int64_t accepted = MainController::lastAcceptedMs.load();
101	    const int64_t any = MainController::lastAnyCsiMs.load();
102	
103	    StatusLight::State state;
104	    std::string text;
105	
106	    if (MainController::captureError.load())
107	    {
108	        state = StatusLight::ERR;
109	        text = "Error - capture failed (NIC/driver)";
110	    }
111	    else if (!MainController::measuringActive.load())
112	    {
113	        state = StatusLight::IDLE;
114	        text = "Idle - not measuring";
115	    }
116	    else if (accepted != 0 && now - accepted < threshold)
117	    {
118	        state = StatusLight::OK;
119	        text = "Capturing target-device CSI";
120	    }
121	    else if (any != 0 && now - any < threshold)
122	    {
123	        state = StatusLight::WARN;
124	        text = "CSI seen - no frames match target filter";
125	    }
126	    else
127	    {
128	        state = StatusLight::ERR;
129	        text = "No CSI - check channel/NIC/transmitter";
130	    }
131	
132	    mainController->statusLight->setState(state, text);
133	    return TRUE;
134	}

262	void MainController::measureCsi(bool stop)
263	{
264	    if (stop)
265	    {
266	        this->measuring = false;
267	        MainController::measuringActive.store(false);
268	        pthread_cancel(this->measureCsiThread);
269	    }
270	    else
271	    {
272	        this->wifiController.setFreq(Arguments::arguments.frequency, Arguments::arguments.bandwidth.c_str());
273	        this->measuring = true;
274	        MainController::captureError.store(false);
275	        MainController::lastAcceptedMs.store(0);
276	        MainController::lastAnyCsiMs.store(0);
277	        MainController::measuringActive.store(true);
278	        pthread_create(&this->measureCsiThread, NULL, &MainController::measureCsi, NULL);
279	        pthread_detach(this->measureCsiThread);
280	    }

326	void MainController::initInterface()
327	{
328	    try
329	    {
330	        this->wifiController.init();
331	        this->wifiController.getInterfaces();
332	        this->wifiController.getPhys();
333	
334	        // delete actual interfaces
335	        for (InterfaceInfo interface : this->wifiController.interfaces)
336	        {
337	            if (Arguments::arguments.verbose)
338	            {
339	                Logger::log(info) << "Remove interface " << interface.ifName << "\n";
340	            }
341	            this->bkpInterfaces.push_back(interface);
342	            this->wifiController.removeInterface(NULL, interface.ifIndex);
343	        }
344	        this->wifiController.createMonitorInteface();
345	        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(500));
346	        this->wifiController.createApInteface();
347	        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(500));
348	    }
349	    catch(const std::exception& e)
350	    {
351	        MainController::captureError.store(true);
352	        if (MainController::mainWindow)
353	        {
354	            MainController::mainWindow->fatalError(e.what());
355	        }
356	        else
357	        {
358	            Logger::log(error) << e.what() << '\n';
359	            delete MainController::INSTANCE;
360	            exit(1);
361	        }
362	    }
363	}
